pin_added.question: "Rerun at 0.65" — but we just recorded that thresholds don't rerun anything. Which of us is wrong?
Nothing in Argus can answer "which knob moved it". Should it?

customData.tooltip: Your words. Note the time: 06:05, not Tuesday — so sometimes you *do* catch it the same morning. The Tuesday case is the one where nothing looked off enough.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: This is a guess you make before you have any evidence — nothing in Argus tells you which source is responsible. Everything downstream of here is you narrowing it down by hand.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: You told me in round 3 that nobody reruns the whole morning by hand. This branch is that, so either it means 'press all three Rerun buttons', or the earlier statement had an exception in it.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
0.65 is a threshold — and we recorded in ADR 0001 that thresholds do not rerun anything, they re-filter what already exists.

So either this step is a slider move you call a rerun, or the ADR is missing something.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**Two tabs and your memory** — your words.

This is the step that does not survive handing the work to someone else, and it is the only step here that Argus does not participate in at all. It also proves the 06:00 numbers are still retrievable: runs sit alongside each other, they are not overwritten.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Drawn as a terminal because that is where your sketch stops — but it is a question, not an answer. Nothing in Argus records what differed between two runs, so this is where the trail goes cold.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The good outcome: the numbers moved because the world moved. Reaching this conclusion currently costs the entire diagram above it.
